**fix(governance): loadBrainConfigOrThrow rejects non-object brain.config.json**

Issue #975: loadBrainConfigOrThrow parsed brain.config.json and returned the result as-is with no shape check, so JSON that parses but is not an object (null, [], 42, "x") was returned unchanged. Every caller reads through optional chaining, so a non-object value degraded exactly like {} - the #942 class (a DENY/exclusion reader fail-open) reached through a shape gap instead of a read/parse failure. Added isPlainObject/describeJsonType helpers and a shape check to loadBrainConfigOrThrow (brain/scripts/lib/brain-config.mjs): throws 'brain.config.json at <path> must contain a JSON object, got <type>' when the parsed value is not a plain object. ENOENT still returns {}; a valid object is unchanged. Measured all 10 loadBrainConfigOrThrow call sites across 8 files (the issue's evidence section names only 6 and does not claim to be exhaustive); proved brain-audit.mjs and approve/cli.mjs fail closed at their real entry points, not just the loader. Classified loadBrainConfig() (the legacy export) for the same gap across its 17 call sites and left it unchanged: none reads a DENY/exclusion list. Mutation table: reverting the shape check turns exactly 8 new tests red (T4-T7 loader-level, 3 in cli.test.mjs, 1 in brain-audit.test.mjs); full suite 5371/5371 green with the fix restored. Drafted (never promoted) a Tier 2 doctrine addendum anchored on the evidence-reader-empty-on-failure.md paragraph as PR #980 (issue #976, still open) will land it.
